title: Type-10 Defender (Elite Dangerous)
intro: The Type-10 Defender by Lakon is the combat version of the Type-9 hull, flown from a bridge with multicrew seats and a fighter pilot seat. It needs a large landing pad and uses the shared HOTAS layout.

panels.name: Type-10 Defender: seats and hardpoints
panels.text: Facts about the Type-10 Defender that set it apart from the other ships: its seats, its weapon mounts and the landing pad size it needs.
panels.context: Everything else in the Type-10 Defender's cockpit works like in every other Elite Dangerous ship.

controls.name: Pilot seat (helm)
controls.text: The pilot's seat of the Type-10 Defender, the helm. Whoever sits here flies the ship and has the whole HOTAS layout of this guide.
controls.context: The Type-10 Defender takes up to four people in all; the other seats are for crew who join in multicrew.

controls.name: Multicrew seats
controls.text: The extra seats of the Type-10 Defender, for up to four crew in all. A friend who joins can sit here as gunner, or as fighter controller when the ship carries a fighter.
controls.context: A gunner works the turreted weapons while the pilot flies; the roles are chosen on the role panel.

controls.name: Fighter pilot seat
controls.text: The seat from which a crew member or a hired pilot flies the small fighter that the Type-10 Defender can carry in a hangar.
controls.context: The fighter is launched and given orders on the role panel; the preset has no HOTAS button for that.

controls.name: Hardpoints (weapon mounts)
controls.text: The weapon mounts of the Type-10 Defender: four large, three medium and two small hardpoints. Bigger mounts take bigger, stronger weapons.
controls.context: The pilot puts the Type-10 Defender's weapons into fire groups on the right panel and fires them with the trigger and the weapon release button.

controls.name: Landing pad size
controls.text: The Type-10 Defender needs a large landing pad or a bigger one. Stations have small, medium and large pads, and small outposts may not have the bigger ones.
controls.context: When the pilot asks a station for docking, the station gives a pad that fits the ship's size.
